title: pfind v3.0.0: gap analysis, STATUS_REPORT ground truth, and --glob bug confirmation

concept.problem_being_solved: Five contradictory status documents existed in the pfind directory, produced by prior agents across this session. They gave completion estimates ranging from 70% to 100%, making it impossible to know the real state of the eza-0.23.5 + ripgrep-15.2.0 merge into pfind.py. The user needed a single reliable answer to: 'have all capabilities been merged?'
concept.approach_taken: Ground-truth extraction from primary sources. Rather than reading the prior status documents, all three sources were interrogated directly: (1) python3 pfind.py --help for the live argparse output, (2) grep of all .rs files in eza-0.23.5/src/ for the canonical eza flag list, (3) grep of all .rs files in ripgrep-15.2.0/ plus rg --help for the ripgrep flag list. Set difference produced the real gap. All five prior documents were superseded by a single STATUS_REPORT.md written from verified evidence.
concept.before_state: Five status documents in /home/gorilla/Documents/Scripts.For.Work/pfind/ gave contradictory completion estimates: STATUS_REPORT.md (old, 70%), IMPLEMENTATION_PROGRESS.md (100%, all tested PASS), CORRECTED_STATUS_REPORT.md (85-90%, untested), REVISED_GAP_ANALYSIS.md (85-90%), PFIND_GAP_ANALYSIS.md (70%). The --glob flag was documented as broken in GLOB_BUG_FINDINGS.md but IMPLEMENTATION_PROGRESS.md still claimed 100% complete. No single document was trustworthy.
concept.after_state: One authoritative STATUS_REPORT.md (343 lines) supersedes all five prior documents. Actual completion is ~80% of the combined eza+ripgrep flag surface from PFIND_SUPER_MERGE_ACTION_PLAN.md: ~82 flags implemented, ~9 partial, ~37 absent. The --glob bug was confirmed fixed in the current pfind.py (args.globs consumers verified at lines 1700, 1715, 1737, 1740, 1849, 1869). pfind.py remains at 1969 lines as uncommitted working-tree changes against git HEAD c6dbb02.
concept.known_alternatives: Not available in the source material. No commit messages document why prior agents chose to produce multiple status documents rather than a single authoritative one. The narrative notes that the prior documents failed because agents read --help output rather than the Rust source trees — but the reason prior agents chose that approach is not documented.

decisions_made.reason: 85-90% (prior agents' best estimate) was rejected because it did not count 6 missing environment variables or partial implementations (--time-style missing long-iso/full-iso, --loc missing =lines|percent|both, archive search missing zip/tar/zst). The 80% figure was derived from counting ~82 implemented, ~9 partial, ~37 absent out of ~128 action-plan items.

decisions_made.reason: Contradictory documents are worse than no documents. A reader who sees both '70% complete' and '100% complete' cannot act. The new STATUS_REPORT.md names each superseded document and explains why it was wrong.

RRF fusion 5-signal formula (name/semantic/content/git/recency) exists in code. Correctness of ranking output was not validated.
--brain semantic seam not tested (requires running Chroma DB).

verification_task.task_title: Verify the STATUS_REPORT.md claims against pfind.py directly

steps.expected_result: Count ≥ 90. Confirms argparse exposes the flags STATUS_REPORT.md claims are implemented.
steps.what_failure_looks_like: Count below 80 would indicate argparse entries were removed or the script has a parse error.

steps.expected_result: Count ≥ 8. Confirms the --glob bug fix is present (args.globs consumed at multiple call sites).
steps.what_failure_looks_like: Count of 0 or 1 means args.globs is still a silent no-op and the glob bug was not fixed.

steps.action: grep -c 'def apply_replacement_preview\|def render_tree_view\|def render_long_table\|def render_grid\|def render_oneline\|class GitStatusCache\|class LocCounts' pfind.py
steps.expected_result: 7. All seven core functions/classes claimed as implemented in STATUS_REPORT.md Section 1 are present.
steps.what_failure_looks_like: Any count below 7 means at least one claimed implementation is absent.

steps.expected_result: 0. Confirms STATUS_REPORT.md Section 2.3 claim that no environment variables are read.
steps.what_failure_looks_like: Any count above 0 means at least one env var IS read, and Section 2.3 is incorrect.

steps.expected_result: Output shows pfind.py as a result with line number. Confirms basic search is functional.
steps.what_failure_looks_like: Python traceback or 'no results' means the tool is broken at the most basic level.

technical_debt.item: v3.0.0 uncommitted for an indeterminate period. Seven hours of merge work exist only in the working tree.
technical_debt.recommendation: git add pfind.py STATUS_REPORT.md && git commit -m 'pfind v3.0.0: super-merge ripgrep-15.2.0 + eza-0.23.5'

technical_debt.item: CHANGELOG in pfind.py header (lines 29-35) claims zip/tar archive support and --level flag — both absent from actual implementation. CHANGELOG is aspirational, not factual.
technical_debt.recommendation: Update CHANGELOG to accurately reflect what is implemented. Move aspirational claims to a ROADMAP section.

technical_debt.item: --time-style only accepts relative|iso|default. eza spec and action plan require long-iso, full-iso, and +FORMAT. format_timestamp() function exists and would need only 3 extra branches.
technical_debt.recommendation: Add long-iso, full-iso, and +FORMAT (strftime passthrough) to format_timestamp() and update argparse choices.

technical_debt.item: Five superseded status documents (STATUS_REPORT.md old, CORRECTED_STATUS_REPORT.md, REVISED_GAP_ANALYSIS.md, PFIND_GAP_ANALYSIS.md, IMPLEMENTATION_PROGRESS.md) still exist in the directory and will confuse future agents.
technical_debt.recommendation: Archive to a superseded/ subdirectory or delete. The new STATUS_REPORT.md explicitly names them as superseded.

glossary.definition: Files on disk before being saved to git. Lost on file deletion; not version-controlled until committed.
Reciprocal Rank Fusion. Combines ranked lists from name, semantic, and content search signals into one ranked output using formula: sum(weight/(k+rank)).
Pure-Python search path used when the rg binary is absent. Slower than ripgrep but produces equivalent output for supported features.
A call site in pfind.py that passes args.globs to rg_common_globs() or _apply_user_globs(). The absence of consumers was the --glob silent bug.
